description_en: The 13-bayphalcāis referred to as Dhaḥmā Phalcā because it houses thedhaḥmās, which serve as the longitudinal main beam of the Matsyendranāth chariot. Adhaḥmā(also sometimes referred to asghaḥmā)is the shaft which is upturned at one end and passes through a chariot between the wheels. There is always a painting of Bhairava on the face of the upturned part. This is covered by a gilt copper image of the same deity. Thedhaḥmāitself is considered to be Karkoṭaka Nāgarāja, the serpent deity who, legend tells, stretched itself across a river from one end to the other, thus enabling the king, a priest and a porter to cross the river when they went to collect Bungadyaḥ. However, the water of this river turned everything that touched it into stone. It was this power that gave it the name Śila Nadi: the stone river. The serpent deity crossed the river after helping the trio. As it crossed it accidentally let the tip of its tail dip into the river. The part that touched the water immediately turned into stone and fell off. This is why the other end of thedhaḥmādoes not have a pointed tip like a serpent's tail (information byRajendra Sakya2015).In 2019, fourdhaḥmāswere kept at thephalcā, one of which was used for the chariot that year. By 2024, only onedhaḥmāfrom the 2019 collection remains, alongside three newer beams now housed there. Thephalcā'selongated and narrow design clearly indicates its purpose of accommodating these lengthy beams. No documented evidence exists regarding the original construction of thephalcā. However, it underwent renovation in 2014 CE by the Lalitpur Municipality in collaboration with the local community. In 2025, only onedhaḥmāis kept inside, another in front of the monument. a third one lies across the small alley close to Samay Phalca.The stretch in front of Dhaḥmā Phalcā was traditionally the initial halt for the chariot procession, but this tradition ceased around 50 years ago. Presently, on the inaugural day, the chariot is drawn directly from Pulchok to Gabāhāḥ. However, an exception occurs every 12 years, when the chariot procession commences from Bungamati, still adhering to the custom of pausing overnight in front of Dhaḥmā Phalcā.An additional room has been constructed at the rear of thephalcāspecifically for storing old chariot wheels. In 1994, the wheels were relocated, and the room was transformed into a gym by a local youth club. Presently, the space has been repurposed by the priests of Buṅgadyaḥ (Pānejus) for organizing feasts. During the journey of the Buṅgadyaḥ chariot to its final destination at Lagankhel (LAL4304andLAL4303), the Pānejus occupy this room overnight.
description_ne: पुल्चोकको व्यस्त सडक छेउमा (पश्चिम) यो फल्चा अवस्थित छ । बुङ्गद्यःको रथमा प्रयोग हुने धःमा संग्रहण गरिने फल्चा भएबाट यसलाई ''धःमा फल्चा'' भन्ने गरिएको छ । यस फल्चाको नजिकै दक्षिणतिर बुङ्गद्यःको रथ बनाउने गरिन्छ । रथ निर्माता बाराही समुहको भनाई अनुसार रथमा सामान्यतः ११ वर्षसम्म एउटै धःमा प्रयोग गर्ने चलन छ । प्रत्यक वर्ष पुनः प्रयोग गरिने धःमालाई जात्रापछि यस फल्चामा ल्याई सुरक्षित राख्ने गरिन्छ । धःमाको आकार समान यो फल्चा लाम्चो आकारमा बनेको छ । करीब ६० फीट लम्बाई भएको फल्चामा १३ कवलहरु रहेका छन् । फल्चाको करीब आधा लम्बाई बराबरको भागमा पछाडिको खण्ड (back wing) पनि बनाइएको छ । उक्त खण्डमा भएको कोठामा बुङ्गद्यःको रथ पुल्चोकमा रहेसम्म पानेजुहरु भोजन गर्ने तथा रात काट्ने गर्दै आएका छन् ।यस फल्चाको निर्माणबारे जानकारी दिने कुनै अभिलेख प्राप्त छैन । वि.सं.२०७१ सालमा ललितपुर उप- महानगरपालिका र स्थानीयको सहकार्यमा फल्चाको जीर्णोद्धारकार्य भएको थियो । फल्चामा हाल ५ वटा धःमाहरु राखिएको देख्न सकिन्छ ।
